subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: The Gambler's Fallacy
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Gambler's Fallacy.

hook.text: A coin lands heads ten times in a row. Most people bet on tails next. But the coin has no memory. It is still 50-50.

buildup.text: In 1913 at the Monte Carlo casino, the ball landed on black 26 times in a row. Gamblers lost millions betting on red.

discovery.text: Each spin is independent. Past outcomes do not change future probabilities. The universe does not balance itself.

twist.text: The gambler's fallacy has a cousin: the hot hand fallacy. We think streaks in basketball predict the next shot.

climax.text: The gambler's fallacy reveals our deep need for patterns. We see balance and order where only randomness exists.

punchline.text: Ten heads in a row? Next flip is still 50-50. Coins have no memory.

quiz.question: What is the gambler's fallacy?
options: Believing past random outcomes affect future independent events
